content_zh:
刘叔皱起眉，叹了口气：“这还真不便宜，小青爷，要想看不出裂痕，就不能局部刷漆，粘合、打磨，这些手工活，我可以一文钱不要你的，只是御用的彩漆每个月都只有定例，我得请采办的额外拨一桶出来，才能修复这木马。你也知道，我是个手艺人，平日又见不着主子的面，只凭二两银子的月例过活，没法承担这桶彩漆的费用啊。”
薛遥绝望地闭上眼。
这下怕是要大出血了。
青河脸色也变了，看出刘叔的胃口不小，便不太客气的问：“要多少钱，您给我个实价，我自然没二话，但要是我承担不起，就只能把木马搬走，出宫再找人想办法。”
青河心里也是有数的，说这话就是想威胁刘叔：别跟宫外木匠要价差太多了，否则可就撕破脸了。
可他毕竟年少，哪有刘叔懂行，知道把这么大一木马运出宫，打点看守都得要几两银子，这大内重重关卡，甚至可能在某道门走不通，竹篮打水一场空。
所以青河这么说，根本威胁不到刘叔。
刘叔算了算将木马运出宫要经过几道门，大概就知道要打点多少银子了，他也没有狮子大开口，只要了打点费用的六成，抬手一比：“得要这个数。”
薛遥警觉地一抬眼，看他比了个四的手势，心里是又郁闷又松了口气。
郁闷的是，这要价至少比宫外高了四倍，松口气的是，四两他还出得起，跟青河一人一半，也就二两银子。
事情得这么想，砸木马，确实是原主薛遥挑的头，按理说，他就是出全部的维修费也说得过去，而维修费市场价是一两银子，他现在要出二两，也不算太坑吧。
薛遥忙着自我安慰，没想到青河却发飙了，抱起木马就要走！
“遥哥儿，走，咱去宫外找人帮忙修吧，四两银子，卖了我也出不起！成不了事，也就被撵出尚书房！”青河面色愤慨地对周围的太监拱手道：“今儿就先跟诸位告个别，来日方长，若是我赵青河未来有那气运金榜题名，再入朝时，必忘不了刘叔对我的‘照顾’！”
居然开始威胁了。
薛遥记得青河学业上并没有什么突出表现，金榜是不可能提名的，小说里也提过他几次，青河长大后跟薛遥一样，成了三皇子府中一位幕僚。
一旁看热闹的太监一听他要被撵出宫，急忙上前劝道：“小青爷别急，价钱又不是死的，都是自己人，采办那边，咱们可以替您去说说嘛！”
说着，为首的太监回过头，目光凶狠地瞪了刘叔一眼，用眼神警告他别太贪心。
青河是他们宫外跑腿的小恩人，这个忙，得诚心诚意的帮。
刘叔却不为所动，他确实只是个手艺人，平时接触不到主子，没有打赏，根本用不着青河帮忙跑腿。
要说交情，也就太监们请青河吃喝的时候，他也能沾上一小口。

刘叔早就眼馋其他人的“意外之财”了，这回好不容易逮到个私活，他哪里能放过宰人的机会？
薛遥见这状况，感觉还有省钱的可能，立即警觉地打量周围埋头干活的小木匠们，疑惑地凑到青河耳边问：“这里又不是只有他一个木匠，咱们就不能换个人问问？”
青河一听这话，就不耐烦地斜了薛遥一眼，明显是觉得他屁事都不懂。
现在连解释的心情都没有，青河抱着木马作势要走，却继续跟那群太监扯皮：“还是不为难刘叔了，只是我实在拿不出四两银子。大家都了解我，平日都给大家忙里忙外，哪怕稍微有点私心，别说四两，四十两我都拿得出，只是没想到，我给别人掏心窝子，别人拿我……”
“小青爷别动怒！”太监们怕真得罪青河，便拿出些实际行动：“这木马，您放在这儿，后天来取，包您搬个崭新的回去，至于银子，您能凑多少，就凑多少，不够的，咱家给您凑齐！”
青河这才停下往外挤的“表演动作”，回头看向说话的太监，感激道：“就这份心意，哪怕事办不成，您这朋友我没白交！”
薛遥听得一愣一愣的，没想到青河这小崽子绕这么大一弯子，想要讨的人情，并不只是对刘叔，而是对这一帮内官监的太监。
看来，青河一开始就是演给所有人看的，铁了心要把这两年送出去的人情收回本，如今也算是达成目的了。

content_en:
Uncle Liu frowned and sighed: "It's really not cheap, Mr. Qing. If you want to see no cracks, you can't partially paint, glue, and polish. I don't want you to pay a penny for these handicrafts. It's just that the royal paint only costs only a penny every month." There is a rule that I have to ask the purchaser to provide an extra bucket to repair this wooden horse. You also know that I am a craftsman and I don’t see my master on weekdays. I only live on two taels of silver a month, so I can’t afford the cost of this bucket of paint.”
Xue Yao closed his eyes in despair.
I'm afraid I'm going to bleed profusely now.
Qinghe's expression also changed. Seeing that Uncle Liu had a big appetite, he asked unkindly: "How much does it cost? Please give me a real price. Of course I won't hesitate. But if I can't afford it, I will have to move the wooden horse away and find someone to find a solution after leaving the palace."
Qinghe knew it well, and said this just to threaten Uncle Liu: Don't ask for too much price difference from the carpenter outside the palace, otherwise you will end up falling out.
But he was still young after all, so Uncle Liu was not as knowledgeable as him. He knew that transporting such a large wooden horse out of the palace would cost a few taels of money to guard it. There were many checkpoints in the palace, and a certain door might even be blocked, and everything would be in vain.
Therefore, what Qing He said could not threaten Uncle Liu at all.
Uncle Liu calculated how many gates he had to go through to transport the wooden horse out of the palace, and he roughly knew how much money it would cost. He was not as open as the lion, so he only wanted 60% of the cost. He raised his hand and said, "This is the amount."
Xue Yao raised his eyes alertly and saw him making a sign of four, feeling depressed and relieved at the same time.
What was depressing was that the asking price was at least four times higher than outside the palace. What was relieved was that he could still afford four taels of silver, and Qing He was half of it, which was only two taels of silver.
You have to think about it this way. The original owner Xue Yao was indeed responsible for smashing the Trojan horse. Logically speaking, it would be reasonable for him to pay the entire maintenance fee. The market price of the maintenance fee is one tael of silver. Now that he wants to pay 2 taels, it is not too cheating.
Xue Yao was busy comforting himself, but unexpectedly Qing He got angry, picked up the wooden horse and was about to leave!
"Brother Yao, let's go and find someone outside the palace to help with the repairs. I can't afford the four taels of silver even if I sell it! If it doesn't work, I will be kicked out of the minister's study!" Qinghe looked angrily and said to the eunuchs around him: "I'll say goodbye to you all now. The days are long. If I, Zhao Qinghe, are named on the luck gold list in the future, I will never forget Uncle Liu's 'care' for me when I enter the court again!"
He actually started to threaten.
Xue Yao remembered that Qinghe did not have any outstanding performance in his studies, and it was impossible to be nominated for the gold list. He was also mentioned several times in the novel. When Qinghe grew up, like Xue Yao, he became an aide in the third prince's house.
When the eunuch who was watching the excitement heard that he was about to be kicked out of the palace, he hurriedly stepped forward to persuade him: "Don't worry, Mr. Qing. The price is not dead. We are all our own people. We can talk to you about where to buy it!"
With that said, the leading eunuch turned around and glared at Uncle Liu fiercely, warning him not to be too greedy.
Qinghe is their little benefactor who runs errands outside the palace. For this task, he must help sincerely.
Uncle Liu was unmoved. He was indeed just a craftsman. He had no contact with his master, no reward, and no need for Qinghe to help him run errands.
When it comes to friendship, when the eunuchs invite Qinghe to eat and drink, he can also get a small bite.
Uncle Liu has been coveting other people's "windfall" for a long time. This time he finally caught someone doing something private. How could he let go of the opportunity to kill people?
Seeing this situation, Xue Yao felt that there was still a possibility of saving money. He immediately looked at the young carpenters around him who were working hard, and asked Qing He in confusion: "He is not the only carpenter here, can't we ask someone else?"
When Qinghe heard this, he glanced at Xue Yao impatiently, obviously thinking that he didn't understand anything.
Now he was not even in the mood to explain. Qinghe hugged the wooden horse and pretended to leave, but continued to argue with the eunuchs: "I still don't want to do it."It's hard for Uncle Liu, but I really can't afford four taels of silver. Everyone knows me, and I work hard for everyone on weekdays. Even if it is a little selfish, I can get away with not to mention four taels, forty taels, but I didn't expect that I would take out others' hearts and others would take advantage of me..."
"Little Qingye, don't be angry! The eunuchs were afraid of offending Qing He, so they took some practical actions: "You can leave this wooden horse here and pick it up the day after tomorrow. I'll give you a brand new one to bring back. As for the money, you can raise as much as you can. If it's not enough, our family will raise it for you!" "
Only then did Qinghe stop the "acting action" of squeezing out, looked back at the eunuch who was speaking, and said gratefully: "With this intention, even if the matter fails, I have not made you a friend in vain! "
Xue Yao was stunned for a moment after hearing this. He didn't expect that this kid Qinghe would go in such a long way. The favor he wanted to get was not just for Uncle Liu, but for this group of eunuchs.
It seems that Qinghe acted for everyone to see from the beginning, and was determined to recoup the favors he had given out in the past two years. Now he has achieved his goal.
